extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for USPTO examiners on when a rejection may properly be made final (including first-action finals), how and when to withdraw finality, setting shortened statutory periods (SSP), advisory actions, examiner's amendments, and the transitional after-final practice under 37 CFR 1.129.

rubrics_metrics.name: No finality when new rejection on newly cited art affects unamended claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action on the merits ... will not be made final if it includes a rejection, on newly cited art, other than information submitted in an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p), of any claim not amended by applicant ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make an Office action final when it contains a new ground of rejection based on newly cited art that applies to claims the applicant did not amend. This prohibition applies even if other claims were amended to require the newly cited art.

rubrics_metrics.name: No finality when new rejection on prior art not of record affects amended claims that introduced expected limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or any subsequent action ... should not be made final if it includes a rejection, on prior art not of record, of any claim amended to include limitations which should reasonably have been expected to be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an applicant amends claims to supply an omitted element or limitation that would reasonably be expected, the examiner should not make the next action final if the examiner introduces a new rejection based on prior art not of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider effect of affidavits/ownership evidence on 102(e)/103 references before making final
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying any 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103 references against an application filed on or after November 29, 1999, the examiner should anticipate that an affidavit (or other adequate proof) averring common ownership at the time the invention was made may disqualify any patent or application applied in a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 103 based on 35 U.S.C. 102(e). If such an affidavit is filed in reply ... and the claims are not amended, the examiner may not make the next Office action final if a new rejection is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is a reasonable likelihood that an applicant will file an affidavit or proof that could disqualify a reference relied on for a 103 rejection based on 102(e), avoid making a subsequent Office action final if a new rejection is introduced; see MPEP § 706.02(l)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner caution when applicant does not point out patentable novelty after amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: In the consideration of claims in an amended case where no attempt is made to point out the patentable novelty, the examiner should be on guard not to allow such claims. The claims may be finally rejected if, in the opinion of the examiner, they are clearly open to rejection on grounds of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant amends claims but fails to identify the patentable distinction, the examiner should scrutinize carefully and may finally reject claims clearly open to rejection under the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Form Paragraph 7.40 when final includes new ground necessitated by amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: Form Paragraph 7.40 should be used where an action is made final including new grounds of rejection necessitated by applicant's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insert ¶7.40 (Action Is Final, Necessitated by Amendment) in final Office actions that include new grounds of rejection that were necessitated by the applicant's amendment; observe SSP language and timing guidance contained in the form paragraph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on using ¶7.40.01 (IDS-with-fee prompted finality)
rubrics_metrics.description: ¶ 7.40.01 Action Is Final, Necessitated by IDS With Fee: Applicant's submission of an IDS under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p) prompted the new ground(s) of rejection presented ... Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use ¶7.40.01 where there is another new ground of rejection introduced by the examiner that was not necessitated by the amendment; insert the filing date of the IDS in bracket 1; do not use in reissue litigation or reexamination cases as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-action final rejection allowed in continuing/substitute applications when claims same and finality applicable
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action in those situations where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application (1) are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application, and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03 for first-action final rejections in these circumstances; ensure the claims are coextensive with earlier application claims and that the same grounds and art would have yielded a final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions: do not make first-action final when new matter or new issues presented in parent after final
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuing or substitute application where that application contains material which was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material denied entry in the parent because it raised new issues or new matter, do not use first-action final form paragraphs; such cases are not proper for immediate finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not make first-action final in CIP when claim includes new subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuation-in-part application where any claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For CIPs with added subject matter not in the parent, a first-action final rejection is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for interview prior to first action should ordinarily be granted
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant interview requests prior to first Office action in continuing/substitute applications as a normal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prematureness of final rejection is a practice question (petitionable, not appealable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any question as to prematureness of a final rejection should be raised, if at all, while the application is still pending before the primary examiner. This is purely a question of practice, wholly distinct from the tenability of the rejection. It may therefore not be advanced as a ground for appeal, or made the basis of complaint before the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences. It is reviewable by petition under 37 CFR 1.181.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues of prematureness must be raised while application is pending; use petition under 37 CFR 1.181 rather than appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw finality on persuasive request for reconsideration (use ¶7.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on request by applicant for reconsideration, the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, he or she should withdraw the finality of the rejection. The finality of the Office action must be withdrawn while the application is still pending. The examiner cannot vacate the final rejection once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.42 (Withdrawal of Finality of Last Office Action) to notify applicant when finality is withdrawn; ensure withdrawal occurs before abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: When final rejection may be withdrawn for new facts/reasons or to apply new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may withdraw the rejection of finally rejected claims. If new facts or reasons are presented such as to convince the examiner that the previously rejected claims are in fact allowable ... the final rejection should be withdrawn. Although it is permissible to withdraw a final rejection for the purpose of entering a new ground of rejection, this practice is to be limited to situations where a new reference either fully meets at least one claim or meets it except for differences which are shown to be completely obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdraw finality if convincing new information shows allowability, or if a new reference fully meets a claim or clearly renders it obvious. Do not withdraw finality merely to apply subsidiary, cumulative, or marginally better references.

rubrics_metrics.name: When finality withdrawn, enter amendments filed after final
rubrics_metrics.description: When a final rejection is withdrawn, all amendments filed after the final rejection are ordinarily entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon withdrawal of finality, normally enter all post-final amendments; be mindful of entry order and conflicting amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: New grounds after appeal require SPE approval
rubrics_metrics.description: New grounds of rejection made in an Office action reopening prosecution after the filing of an appeal brief require the approval of the supervisory patent examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain SPE approval before issuing new grounds in actions reopening prosecution post-appeal brief filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set variable SSP language in final rejections (3-month default, variable if first reply within 2 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: All final rejections setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply should contain one of form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.40.01, 7.41, or 7.41.03 advising applicant that if the reply is filed within 2 months ... the shortened statutory period will expire at 3 months ... or on the date the advisory action is mailed, whichever is later. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate form paragraphs to implement the variable SSP mechanism; ensure applicant is notified and that the reply deadline cannot exceed 6 months from the final rejection date.

rubrics_metrics.name: If variable-SSP paragraph omitted, SSP is 3 months and only extendable by petition
rubrics_metrics.description: If the form paragraph setting a variable reply period is inadvertently not included in the final Office action, the SSP for reply will end 3 months from the date of the final Office action and cannot be extended other than by making a petition and paying a fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a). However, if an advisory action is mailed in such a case where the reply to the final action has been filed within 2 months, the examiner should vacate the original SSP and reset the period for reply ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the variable-SSP paragraph is omitted, treat SSP as 3 months; if applicant timely files first reply within 2 months and an advisory action is later mailed, vacate original SSP and reset per policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure limitations: SSP mechanism not applicable where SSP < 3 months
rubrics_metrics.description: This procedure of setting a variable reply period ... does not apply to situations where a SSP less than 3 months is set, e.g., reissue litigation applications (1-month SSP) or any reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to apply variable-SSP rules where statute/regulation sets a shorter SSP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action determinations when first reply filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period ... AND applicant files a complete first reply to the final Office action within 2 months ... the examiner must determine if the reply: (1) places the application in condition for allowance — then process as allowance; (2) places the application in condition for allowance except for matters of form which the examiner can change without authorization — amend and process as allowance; or (3) does not place the application in condition for allowance — then notify applicant that the SSP expires 3 months from the date of the final rejection or as of the mailing date of the advisory action, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PTOL-303 or Form Paragraph 7.67.01 for advisory actions when first complete reply is filed within 2 months; decide among the three outcomes and proceed accordingly, waiving extension fees when allowance results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Form Paragraph 7.67 when no complete first reply within 2 months under variable SSP
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action sets a variable reply period ... and applicant does NOT file a complete first reply to the final Office action within 2 months, examiners should use Form Paragraph 7.67.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue the appropriate advisory action using Form Paragraph 7.67 when applicant fails to file a complete first reply within two months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vacate/reset SSP when no variable SSP set but applicant filed timely reply and advisory delayed
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the final Office action does not set a variable reply period ... AND applicant does file a complete first reply to the final Office action within 2 months, and if an advisory action is necessary and cannot be mailed within 3 months of the final Office action, the examiner should vacate the original SSP and reset the reply period to expire on the mailing date of the advisory action by using form paragraph 7.67.02. In no case can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the advisory action will be late, vacate an incorrectly-set original SSP and reset to advisory mailing date; do not allow reply period to extend beyond 6 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of time for further action and calculation of extension fees after advisory
rubrics_metrics.description: When an advisory action properly contains either form paragraph 7.67.01 or 7.67.02, the time for applicant to take further action ... begins to run 3 months from the date of the final rejection, or from the date of the advisory action, whichever is later. Extension fees cannot be prorated for portions of a month. In no event can the statutory period for reply expire later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute extension fees and reply deadlines according to advisory/form paragraph timing; apply the 'whichever is later' rule between final rejection date and advisory mailing date, and cap at six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendment without extension fees when first reply timely filed within 2 months
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, an examiner’s amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without the payment of extension fees even if the examiner’s amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of the final Office action. Note that an examiner’s amendment may not be made more than 6 months from the date of the final Office action, as the application would be abandoned at that point by operation of law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant files the first complete reply within two months, the examiner may make amendments to place the case in condition for allowance without requiring extension fees, subject to the six-month absolute limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant authorization and extension fees when first reply not timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a complete first reply to a final Office action has not been filed within 2 months of the final Office action, applicant’s authorization to make an amendment to place the application in condition for allowance must be made either within the 3 month shortened statutory period or within an extended period for reply that has been petitioned and paid for by applicant pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a). However, an examiner’s amendment correcting only formal matters ... would not require any extension fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant misses the two-month timely reply, obtain either authorization within the SSP or an extension petition and fee before making substantive examiner’s amendments to place case in allowance; formal corrections identified for the first time after reply do not require extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires petition and fee; examiner may be authorized to file
rubrics_metrics.description: An extension of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) requires a petition for an extension and the appropriate fee provided for in 37 CFR 1.17. Where an extension of time is necessary to place an application in condition for allowance ... applicant may file the required petition and fee or give authorization to the examiner to make the petition of record and charge a specified fee to a deposit account. When authorization to make a petition of record is given to the examiner, the authorization must be given before the extended period expires. The authorization must be made of record in an examiner’s amendment by indicating the name of the person making the authorization, when the authorization was given, the deposit account number to be charged, the length of the extension requested and the amount of the fee to be charged to the deposit account. Form Paragraph 13.02.02 should be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure petitions and fees for extensions are properly filed or that the applicant's authorization is recorded per Form Paragraph 13.02.02 with all required account and authorization details before the extended period expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replies after final must be processed promptly and only considered if within SSP or with petition/fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly by all Office personnel. Replies after final should not be considered by the examiner unless they are filed within the SSP or are accompanied by a petition for an extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 37 CFR 1.136(a)). This requirement also applies to supplemental replies filed after the first reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not consider after-final replies unless timely or accompanied by the correct petition and fee; process any timely replies without undue delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews after SSP may occur within 6-month statutory period without extension fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after the expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply to a final Office action but within the 6-month statutory period for reply without the payment of an extension fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews occurring after the SSP but before the six-month statutory deadline are permissible without requiring payment of extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex parte Quayle practice for formal matters identified after reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal matters which are identified for the first time after a reply is made to a final Office action and which require action by applicant to correct may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance. No extension fees would be required since the reply puts the application in condition for allowance except for the correction of formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only formal corrections remain, use Ex parte Quayle practice and do not require extension fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw finality when reopening prosecution after a reply to avoid abandonment/fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution is to be reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid the issue of abandonment and the payment of extension fees. For example, if a new reference comes to the attention of the examiner which renders unpatentable a claim indicated to be allowable, the Office action should begin with a statement to the effect: 'The finality of the Office action mailed is hereby withdrawn in view of the new ground of rejection set forth below.' Form Paragraph 7.42 could be used in addition to this statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reopening prosecution after a post-final reply, withdraw finality (and notify applicant) to prevent inadvertent abandonment and to avoid unnecessary extension-fee assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice eligibility under 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in an application, other than for reissue or a design patent, that has been pending for at least two years as of June 8, 1995 ... is entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection under the following circumstances: The Office will consider such a submission, if the first submission and the fee set forth in § 1.17(r) are filed prior to the filing of an appeal brief and prior to abandonment ... The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon the timely filing of the submission and payment of the fee set forth in § 1.17(r).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 37 CFR 1.129(a) only to eligible applications pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (not reissue or design apps); accept first and second submissions upon timely payment of the §1.17(r) fee and automatically withdraw finality when fee/submission properly filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice limited to applications filed on or before June 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: The transitional after-final practice is only available to applications filed on or before June 8, 1995 and it is not available for reissue or design applications or reexamination proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not apply 37 CFR 1.129(a) to applications filed after June 8, 1995, or to reissue, design, or reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) may not introduce new matter and previously refused IDS considered if fee paid
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment considered as a result of payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) may not introduce new matter into the disclosure of the application. Any IDS previously refused consideration because of applicant's failure to comply with 37 CFR 1.97(c) or (d) will be treated as though it has been filed within one of the time periods set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(b) and will be considered without the petition and petition fee required in 37 CFR 1.97(d), if it complies with 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submissions under 1.129(a) do not add new matter. If the §1.17(r) fee is paid, previously refused IDSs may be entered and considered as timely (subject to 1.98 compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission under 1.129(a) yields one-month SSP to submit complete reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If, upon timely payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), the examiner determines that the submission is not fully responsive to the previous Office action ... applicant will be given a shortened statutory period of 1 month or 30 days, whichever is longer, to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a 1.129(a) submission is not fully responsive, issue Form Paragraph 7.42.02 stating reasons and give applicant a one-month (or 30-day) shortened statutory period to file a complete reply; this period may be extended under 37 CFR 1.136(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Following payment under 1.129(a), next merits action may be made final only under first-action-final conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: After submission and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r), the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a final action follows a 1.129(a) submission and fee, ensure that any first-action final follows the requirements described for first-action final rejections in continuing/substitute applications (see ¶7.41.03 and ¶7.41 conditions).
